_what: The ONLY authored input to 4D scheduling. Everything else is EXTRACTED — phase order from sequence_rules.json's min sequence per phase, trades from the union of that phase's classes' resources, level from ScheduleGate.deriveBandRanks, work from ScheduleAuthor._installSecs, crews from LABOR_RATES.max_crews, shift from rates.js SHIFT_HOURS. Spec: bim-compiler prompts/4D_BAR_MODEL.md §4.
_replaces: 4D_template.json v1.2.0, which was 123 lines and 146 keys — 52 of them prose, and its data keys were copies: phases[].sequence and phases[].trades duplicated sequence_rules.json, its ten dependency edges restated the phase list order plus one flag, and `scope` and `replicate_per_level` were the same fact twice with an invariant written to check they agreed instead of deleting one. Audited 2026-08-25 on the user's observation that it was 'not even a recipe yet, it is just a mould — an extraction'.
_days_per_week_why: Matches what the engine does today (schedule_gate.js applies no week calendar; §CREW_DAY logs '24/7 calendar unchanged'). Stated so a 5-day week is an edit, not a rewrite. Hours per shift is NOT here — rates.js SHIFT_HOURS already owns it (user ruling 2026-08-13, 24h default).
_phase_link_why: USER RULING 2026-08-25: 'we make phases packed but sequential? User can then just drag them overlap if they want.' FS+0 between consecutive phases on a level. An overlap is a human's drag on the Gantt, never a solver artifact. Priced before adopting: 49d vs the overlapping engine's 46.9d on HHS_Office_Federated, +4%.
_level_link_why: §4D_BAND_MONOTONIC — 'a trade may not run ahead of ITSELF on the floor below'. Enforced PER TRADE, on the emitted times, not by chaining whole level TASKS. The task ladder was stricter than the ruling it implemented: it made every trade in a task wait for every trade in the task below, and paid for that in midair. MEASURED 2026-08-25, task ladder -> trade ladder: Hospital midair 228 -> 92 and band inversions 7 -> 4; Terminal 413 -> 336 and 14 -> 4; HHS 86 -> 70 and 1 -> 0; Duplex 14 -> 12 and 1 -> 1. Better on BOTH axes on every building — there was no trade-off, only an over-tight constraint. Different trades still overlap across floors, which is what a trade train IS. Without any ladder at all: Hospital band inversions 48,589. Value 'self' restores the old whole-task chain.
_level_bands_why: The GRANULARITY DIAL. 'storey' = one band per real storey (finest). An integer coarsens to that many bands by rank. The two hells trade against each other smoothly and level granularity is the exchange rate. MEASURED 2026-08-25 — Terminal (22 storeys): 22 bands -> midair 336 / band inversions 4; 11 -> 219/7,074; 6 -> 86/13,996; 3 -> 51/15,535; 1 -> 0/29,993. Hospital (8): 8 -> 92/4; 4 -> 32/25,319; 1 -> 22/48,589. Fine = strict floor-by-floor trade discipline with some floating; coarse = clean build-up with no floating and trades free to roam vertically. Both ends come from the SAME graph and the SAME composite — one number changes, the model does not fork, so there is still exactly one stored timeline and nothing to reconcile. DEFAULT is 'storey' because §4D_BAND_MONOTONIC is a user ruling from watching upper floors get walled first, not a preference to trade away for a nicer number. NOTE: a proper merge of naming-variant storeys (Terminal has 'Ceiling Level 04', 'Aras Tanah', '04 THIRD FLOOR LEVEL') needs §S18 deriveStoreyMergeMap, which needs IfcBuildingStorey.Elevation — ABSENT from all four shipped DBs, so this dial is the interim control.
_ceiling_link_why: A level's fit-out hangs from the ceiling above it, and that ceiling IS the floor slab of the level above. Every other edge in this model points DOWN or sideways (phases chain within a level; a phase waits for itself one level below), so nothing said 'Level 1's services wait for Level 2's frame' and the scheduler placed pipes under an unbuilt slab. MEASURED 2026-08-25 without this edge: of Hospital's 9,911 premature placements, 6,724 were MEP Rough-in waiting on Superstructure ON THE LEVEL ABOVE and 1,360 were Architecture doing the same; Duplex 282 of 329. It is a missing edge, not bad data — the frame runs ahead of the fit-out on every real site. Value 'frame_above' makes every non-structural phase on level N wait for Superstructure on level N+1. 'none' restores the old behaviour.
_building_scope_why: Phases that occur ONCE for the whole building instead of repeating per storey. Their TaskBar hangs off the ProjectBar, never off a LevelBar — hanging it under one level made its bar span every level and overlap that level's own tasks (measured as 2/34 false phase-stacking pairs on Duplex in the 2026-08-25 prototype). Their elements are collected from EVERY level: dropping the ones above the lowest silently lost an element on Hospital, 63,181 of 63,182, invisible in every other number.
